title: Measure the expert's retention-feedback latency budget
hypothesis: Delaying pen-state feedback by four control steps makes the qualified expert's retention corrections arrive too late, reducing sustained Stage-3 success despite live proprioception and action history.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the unmodified qualified PPO expert on identical placements; a 0.25 decrease would establish a practically important feedback-bandwidth requirement for symbolic controllers. Unlike D-040's constant clamps, this intervention supplies genuine past observations and tests timing rather than feature removal.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study feedback_delay --manifest-seed 4200 --output-dir logs/pen_spin_feedback_delay_s4200"'
code_changes: scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py: add the declared feedback_delay study CLI; freeze 40 fresh Stage-3 placements before evaluation and run unmodified, independent unmodified repeat, four-step pen-state delay, and four-step hand-state delay in separate processes.

scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py: delay only the named observation groups, keep action history live, initialize each history buffer from its own reset observation, and assert unchanged observations outside the delayed group.

config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml: register the qualified expert, frozen sustained-success reducer, paired analysis, and existing reproducibility acceptance rule; report drop timing and explicitly retain the temporal joint-distribution-shift limitation.

falsified_by: With verified delay injection and passing reproducibility controls, a paired interval entirely above -0.25 refutes the predicted decrease; an interval crossing -0.25 is inconclusive.

approval.note: This tests feedback timing rather than repeating D-040's constant-clamp intervention, with independent repeats and hand-delay controls. At 160 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls, it is the cheapest informative next experiment. Its weakest point is temporal distribution shift: the result character

direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This tests feedback timing rather than repeating D-040's constant-clamp intervention, with independent repeats and hand-delay controls. At 160 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls, it is the cheapest informative next experiment. Its weakest point is temporal distribution shift: the result characterizes this expert, not a universal bandwidth requirement for symbolic controllers. With verified injection and passing reproducibility controls, an interval wholly above -0.25 falsifies the predicted paired_success_difference decrease of at least 0.25 against the unmodified expert.

implementer.reasoning: Cheap (160 episodes, 0 calls) and it reuses the R-044 lesion machinery: a delayed real observation tests timing rather than removal. I will implement it as a DelayedController beside LesionedController, with the same reproducibility gate, and report drop timing; the limitation that it characterizes this checkpoint under temporal distribution shift is kept.
